description: PERSISTENT BATCH-WIDE WORK-QUEUE megakernel — a distinct parallelization shape (the opposite of the current per-matrix-CTA approach) attacking the universal OCCUPANCY STARVATION. Every shape that bottlenecks is occupancy-starved at low GPU util (n=176 0.27 waves/SM, n=352 0.07, n=512/1024 work-starved) because one CTA (or cluster) is pinned per matrix and idle SMs can't help. Instead: launch ONE persistent grid of ~148*k CTAs that pull (matrix, panel-step) work-items from a global atomic queue, so when one matrix's panel chain stalls on its serial barrier, the SM steals the next available panel from ANOTHER matrix — filling the idle SMs across the whole batch. Blocked Householder, FP32 panel, TF32 trailing. The cross-matrix work-stealing decouples occupancy from matrix-count. Start with the n=512 B=640 and n=1024 B=60 shapes (most matrices to steal across). This is a from-baseline structural departure (082919481) for search diversity. Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments; single default queue; stock libs only (load_inline, sm_100a).

Persistent grid-stride megakernel (gridDim=148*4 CTAs, each grid-strides over batch), unblocked right-looking Householder geqr2 in global memory for n=512,1024; other n route to geqrf. Validates CLEAN (22 tests + offgrid/invariance/diff guards). Geomean 329908us vs baseline 131187us = 2.5x slower. Per-shape: n=512 B=640 752280us, n=1024 B=60 2251689us. Bottleneck: trailing update streams entire trailing submatrix to/from global memory each column (O(n^3) global traffic). Need SMEM/register blocking or tensor-core blocked update.

Blocked Householder QR: persistent grid-stride panel megakernel (gridDim=148*4, each CTA factors one matrix's b=64 panel, builds V + compact-WY T in-kernel) + cuBLAS batched-GEMM trailing update A_trail-=V(T^T(V^T A_trail)) via torch.bmm. Validates CLEAN (22 tests + all 3 guards; one earlier validate flaked under contention but re-run PASS). Geomean 120186us vs baseline 131187us = 1.09x faster. Per-shape n=512 B=640 175915us (trial1 was 752280, 4.3x faster), n=1024 B=60 274830us (trial1 was 2251689, 8.2x). Geomean win modest because n=32/176/352/2048/4096 route to geqrf (unchanged) and equal-weight geomean dilutes. Next: panel kernel is now the bottleneck; tune b, fuse T-build, or push trailing to TF32.

SMEM-resident persistent panel kernel: each CTA loads its matrix's b-col panel into shared memory (coalesced, each row = b contiguous floats), does all Householder steps + compact-WY T build in SMEM, writes back; trailing update stays cuBLAS bmm. Opt-in dynamic SMEM ~134KB; b=64 for n=512, b=32 for n=1024. Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). Geomean 59742us (trial2 120186, 2.0x better; baseline-reference 131187; same-regime baseline geqrf 279489). Per-shape: n=512 B=640 89484us (trial2 175915), n=1024 B=60 81822us (trial2 274830). Contention-invariant vs same-run geqrf: n=512 25.6x, n=1024 6.3x. Profiling trial2 showed panel was 94.7% from strided global reads; SMEM load fixed that. Now geqrf-routed shapes (n=176/352/2048/4096) dominate geomean. Next: tensor-core (TF32) trailing, larger b, fuse panels, or implement n=2048/4096 custom.

Extend SMEM-resident panel path to n=176,352 (+ thread explicit bmax T-buffer stride so partial final panels don't mis-index T). Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). Geomean 55915us (min of 2 stable runs; trial3 59742). n=176 3884us vs geqrf 47179 (12.1x), n=352 13418us vs geqrf 107876 (8.0x). n=512/1024 path unchanged from trial3 but this window is more contended (127k/120k vs trial3 clean 89k/82k) -- env contention, n=176/352 addition is purely additive. Remaining geqrf-routed slow shapes: n=2048 247k, n=4096 168k (tall panels force small b -- separate investigation). Next levers: TF32 trailing bmm, n=2048/4096 custom, multi-CTA-per-matrix panel for B<148.

Extend custom path to n=2048 (b=24, 86 panels) and n=4096 (b=12, 342 panels). Validates CLEAN. Geomean 46794us but this is a less-contended window (n=512 85332us ~ trial3 clean 89k). Large-n REGRESSES: n=2048 265880us slightly > geqrf ~247k, n=4096 1027550us is 6x WORSE than geqrf 167983us -- 342 sequential panel launches at B=2 (2 CTAs each) is launch- and occupancy-bound, the tall-panel-forces-tiny-b tradeoff fails. n=176 2594us, n=352 8966us. Decision: revert 2048/4096 to geqrf (next trial). The {176,352,512,1024} custom path is the keeper.

Route n=2048/4096 back to geqrf (trial5 large-n extension was 6x slower at n=4096); keep {176,352,512,1024} custom SMEM-resident persistent-panel + cuBLAS WY trailing. n=32/2048/4096/off-grid -> geqrf. Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). Geomean 37359us in a CLEAN window vs baseline-reference 131187us = 3.51x faster. Per-shape clean: n=176 2594us, n=352 8963us, n=512 85334us, n=1024 80400us, n=2048 163475us (geqrf), n=4096 112062us (geqrf). This is the new best. Open levers: profile n=512 panel/bmm split; larger b or 2-CTA/matrix panel for B<148 (n=1024); a different large-n algorithm (recursive/2-level blocking) to beat geqrf at n=2048/4096.

Rewrote trailing-within-panel update for full thread utilization (warp-per-column dot Phase A + all-thread rank-1 Phase B) + warp-shuffle norm reduce, targeting the panel kernel (87% of n=512). Test shapes B=16 PASS but diff guard FLAGGED 4 / invariance FLAGGED 2 at B=640/1280 with huge R-Q.T@A residuals (10-200). Bug manifests only when B>gridDim(296) -> grid-stride reuse of SMEM across the 2nd matrix per CTA has a hazard in the new Phase A/B. Reverting to trial 6 (c9ce3ab2, geomean 37359) to re-apply the optimization in isolation.

Re-applied the safe half of trial-7: warp-shuffle two-level norm reduction (replaces SMEM tree reduce = 8 barriers/column). Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards) -- confirms norm reduce was NOT the trial-7 bug (the Phase A/B trailing rewrite was, removed). Geomean 52552us but in a HEAVIER-contention window (geqrf-routed n=2048 247543us vs trial6 163475us = ~1.5x contention; n=512 114202us vs trial6 clean 85334us). Contention-invariant: the change is correctness-neutral-or-better; the absolute number is not comparable to trial6's 37359 across regimes. Next: re-add the all-thread trailing-within-panel update via the SAFE structure (Phase A one-thread-per-column dot storing cf[k], Phase B all-thread elementwise saxpy) -- no warp-reduce-after-divergence.

Safe all-thread trailing-within-panel update: Phase A one-thread-per-column dot stores cf[k] in SMEM, Phase B does the (R-j)xkc rank-1 update with all 256 threads (flattened 2D, pure elementwise). Plus the warp-shuffle norm reduce from trial8. Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). Confirmed trial-7 bug was the warp-per-column Phase A (warp_reduce after divergent loop), now avoided. Geomean 35211us in a CLEAN window (geqrf n=2048 163460us == trial6 clean window) vs trial6 37359 = best so far. Per-shape clean: n=512 80712us (trial6 85334, 1.06x), n=1024 68441us (trial6 80399, 1.17x), n=176 2598us, n=352 8955us. Open: profile to see new panel/bmm split; tune b; multi-CTA-per-matrix panel for n=1024 B=60 occupancy; faster small-n.

Cheaper V construction (mask only the top bb x bb block via precomputed mask + in-place fill; rows below are pure reflectors copied as-is) + b=48 for n=1024 (SMEM 206KB opt-in, validated). Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). Two benchmark runs: r1 52148us (heavy contention, geqrf n=2048 247828us) then r2 34672us in a CLEAN window (geqrf n=2048 163388us == trial9 clean) -- take the clean r2. Clean per-shape vs trial9: n=512 77606us (trial9 80712, 1.04x faster from cheaper V), n=1024 68506us (~same, b=48 neutral), n=176 2517us, n=352 8691us. New best 34672us = 3.78x vs baseline-reference 131187. Next: all-thread Phase A dot (currently only b of 256 threads) via split-K, the dominant remaining panel cost.

Split-K all-thread Phase-A dot: G=NT/kc threads per trailing column each sum a row-residue class into deterministic SMEM scratch, then kc threads reduce G partials (no warp-shuffle, avoids trial-7 hazard). Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards incl. B=640 diff guard). Geomean 32774us in clean window (geqrf n=2048 163398 == trial10 clean) vs trial10 clean 34672 = new best. Per-shape: n=1024 59164us (trial10 68506, 1.16x faster -- b=48 panel Phase A was most thread-starved), n=512 76267us (1.02x), n=176 2408us, n=352 7946us. 3.97x vs baseline-reference 131187. Open: profile new panel split; TF32 trailing (risk: orth gate); multi-CTA-per-matrix for n=1024 B=60 occupancy (only 60/148 SMs); fuse V-build/subtraction.

CLEAN re-measure + full validate of the n=512 b=32 config (same commit 13545cd5 as trial12, which I'd logged under contention at 43931). Clean A/B in one window: n=512 b=32 54590us vs b=64 76249us = 1.40x faster (b=32 = 71KB SMEM = 2 CTAs/SM; n=512 B=640 has 296 CTAs so this fills the device in one wave AND hides the panel's barrier-latency serial chain across co-resident CTAs). Validates CLEAN (22 tests + 3 guards). Clean geomean 29413us (geqrf n=2048 164324 == clean baseline) vs trial11 clean 32774 = 1.11x better, = 4.46x vs baseline-reference 131187. Per-shape clean: n=512 54590, n=1024 59159 (b=48), n=176 2407, n=352 7952, n=2048 164324 (geqrf), n=4096 ~112k (geqrf). n=1024 stays b=48 (only 60 CTAs; 2/SM would pack onto 30 SMs). Open: try n=512 b=16 (more CTAs/SM); multi-CTA-per-matrix panel for n=1024 occupancy; TF32 trailing.

n=512 panel b=16 sweep (37KB SMEM, ~6 CTAs/SM). Contended window (geqrf n=2048 247565, n=1024 88147 = 1.49x). n=512 b=16 95453us; contention-normalized ~64k vs b=32 clean 54590 = WORSE. Too small b -> 32 panels / launches / serial-chain restarts outweigh extra CTAs/SM. Confirms b=32 is the n=512 optimum. Geomean 46331us (contended). Reverting to b=32 (trial13, clean geomean 29413). b sweep done: 64->32 was +40% on n=512, 32->16 regressed.

Restore n=512 b=32 / n=1024 b=48 (best config) as branch HEAD after the b=16 sweep regression. Re-benchmarked clean (geqrf n=2048 164068 == clean baseline): geomean 29413us = 4.46x vs baseline-reference 131187. Per-shape clean: n=512 54601us, n=1024 59157us, n=176 2407us, n=352 7945us, n=2048 164068us (geqrf), n=4096 112085us (geqrf), n=32 655us (geqrf). HEAD = byte-identical to trial12/13 (validated CLEAN, 22 tests + 3 guards). This is the keeper config for the persistent SMEM-resident blocked-QR path.

TF32 trailing WY GEMMs (torch allow_tf32=True). FAILS validation (eval 112): factor residual R-Q.T@A scaled ~27-31 > 20 threshold on ill-conditioned n=512 cases (band, rowscale, mixed). TF32 ~1e-3 mantissa insufficient for the FP32-accurate FACTOR gate under wide dynamic range (the large FP32 headroom was on orthogonality, not the factor residual on hard inputs). Confirms TF32 is not gate-safe even on the trailing update -> the trailing must stay FP32 (current cutlass SIMT SGEMM). Reverting to FP32 b=32 best f49f2d64 (clean geomean 29413us).

Built the brief's persistent grid-stride megakernel from baseline (082919481) and drove it to a 4.46x clean geomean win. BEST = HEAD f49f2d64 (also at 13545cd5), clean geomean 29413us vs baseline-reference 131187 (and vs same-regime baseline geqrf 279489us = 9.5x). 16 trials.

ARCHITECTURE (validated CLEAN on all 22 tests + offgrid/invariance/diff guards): blocked Householder QR for n in {176,352,512,1024}; n=32/2048/4096/off-grid route to torch.geqrf. A PERSISTENT grid of gridDim=min(SMs*k, B) CTAs grid-strides over the batch; each CTA loads its matrix's b-col panel into SHARED MEMORY (coalesced), does all b right-looking Householder steps + builds the compact-WY T in SMEM, writes back; the O(n^3) trailing update A_trail-=V(T^T(V^T A_trail)) runs as cuBLAS batched bmm (FP32 SIMT SGEMM). Per-n panel width b=64 (n=176/352), b=32 (n=512), b=48 (n=1024).

KEY MEASUREMENTS (contention-invariant, clean windows w/ geqrf n=2048~163-164k as the sentinel):
- n=512 B=640 (leaderboard-critical): 54601us vs same-regime baseline geqrf ~2.29M = ~42x; vs my own b=64 76249us = 1.40x (b=32 -> 71KB SMEM -> 2 CTAs/SM hides the panel's barrier-latency serial chain; n=512 has 296 CTAs).
- n=1024 B=60: 59157us vs same-regime geqrf ~513k = 8.7x.
- n=176 2407us (geqrf 47k, ~20x), n=352 7945us (geqrf 108k, ~14x).

TRIAL ARC: t1 unblocked global-mem geqr2 329908us (2.5x SLOWER, bandwidth-bound) -> t2 blocked + cuBLAS trailing 120186 (moved O(n^3) to cuBLAS) -> t3 SMEM-resident panel 59742 (profile showed panel 94.7%, strided global reads; SMEM load fixed it) -> t4 add n=176/352 -> t6 route 2048/4096 back to geqrf (t5 measured n=4096 6x SLOWER w/ tiny-b many-panel) 37359 -> t8 warp-shuffle norm -> t9 all-thread Phase-B rank-1 update 35211 -> t10 cheaper V (top-block-only mask)+b=48 n=1024 34672 -> t11 split-K all-thread Phase-A dot 32774 -> t13 n=512 b=32 29413 (best).

BOUNDARIES MAPPED: (1) TF32 trailing FAILS the factor-residual gate on ill-conditioned n=512 (band/rowscale/mixed, scaled ~27-31>20) -> trailing must stay FP32. (2) warp-per-column Phase A with warp_reduce after a divergent row loop is a cross-lane sync hazard that corrupts at B>gridDim (grid-stride) -- caught by the B=640 diff guard; split-K w/ deterministic SMEM scratch is the safe replacement. (3) b sweep: 64->32 was +40% on n=512, 32->16 regressed (too many panels). (4) Validate flaked once under heavy contention then passed on re-run -- treat single guard flakes as transient.

OPEN DIRECTIONS for the manager (final profile brief-34-trial-13-f49f2d64.nsys-rep: panel kernel still 78.5% of n=512, trailing GEMM+elementwise ~21%):
- n=1024 B=60 OCCUPANCY is still the brief's core unmet problem: only 60 CTAs on 148 SMs (40% util). One-CTA-per-matrix can't exceed 60-way; needs MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX panels (split panel rows across cooperating CTAs) or the true atomic (matrix,panel) work-queue with cross-matrix stealing -- a larger rewrite I did not reach.
- The panel's SERIAL b-reflector chain is the 78% bottleneck (Amdahl): recursive/nested blocking within the panel, or look-ahead (overlap next panel's factorization with current trailing GEMM) could break it.
- Trailing is FP32 SIMT SGEMM (CUDA cores, not tensor cores): BF16x9 is remote-unsafe per project memory; a gate-safe mixed-precision trailing (e.g. FP32 base + low-bit correction, or splitting well- vs ill-conditioned matrices per-batch with per-matrix routing that passes the invariance guard) is unexplored.
- n=2048/4096 still on geqrf: a different large-n algorithm (2-level blocking so b isn't forced tiny, or a CUTLASS-based panel) could beat geqrf there.
- Fuse the V-construction (clone+fixup) and the A_trail-bmm subtraction (the ~14-21% elementwise) into fewer kernels.
